changes.after: Save a draft and read it back, while handling missing or damaged data.

before: localStorage stores strings for one origin in a browser. It is not cloud sync, and users or browser policies can clear or block it.
setItem(key, text) writes a string. getItem(key) returns the stored string or null when no entry exists.
This practice receives a storage object with getItem and setItem methods. Tests supply an in-memory adapter; they do not prove real browser persistence.
After reading a record, parse it and check its shape. Saved data may be old or damaged even if your current writer is correct.
Both storage access and JSON parsing can throw. Wrap those operations in try/catch and choose an honest failure result.
For a real browser companion, obtain window.localStorage inside try/catch before calling these helpers. Accessing the property itself can fail. Never store passwords or secrets here.
The practice saves JSON shaped as {text: yourText}. saveDraft returns true only after writing succeeds; loadDraft returns a string or null for missing, broken, or wrongly shaped data.
saveDraft accepts only a string. Reject other values with false before attempting to write; empty text is a valid draft.
after:
`localStorage` saves text in a browser for one origin: the same address scheme, host, and port.

It can keep data after a page reload, but it is not cloud sync. Users or browser settings can clear or block it.

`setItem(key, text)` saves text under a key. `getItem(key)` reads it back, or gives `null` when the key is missing.

An empty string is saved text. It is different from a missing entry.

The practice functions receive a storage object with `getItem` and `setItem` methods.

The checks use a small in-memory stand-in. That lets us test success and failure without changing your browser's saved data.

Check loaded data before using it. An old or damaged record might have the wrong shape.

For a draft, require a non-null record with a `text` property whose type is string.

Reading, writing, or parsing can throw an error. Put these operations inside `try` and handle failures in `catch`.

Return `false` when saving fails. Return `null` when loading cannot produce a valid draft. Do not report a failed write as saved.

On a real page, read `window.localStorage` inside `try` too. Even access to that property can be blocked.

Use browser storage for suitable local preferences or drafts, not passwords or secrets.

Complete `saveDraft(storage, text)` and `loadDraft(storage)` using the key `draft`.

Save JSON containing `{text: yourText}`. Return `true` only after writing succeeds. Loading returns the saved string, or `null` for missing, broken, or wrongly shaped data.

Accept only strings when saving. Return `false` for other types before attempting a write.

An empty string is valid. Check its type rather than whether it is truthy.

changes.before: The automatic exercise uses supplied storage adapters, not window.localStorage. To verify persistence, serve your own page from a normal web origin, wrap access to window.localStorage in try/catch, save a harmless draft, reload and read it. Browser policy, private mode, clearing site data and storage limits may change availability; this is not phone/computer synchronization.

headings: Try storage on your own page

project.title: Save and read browser data safely
project.task: Complete saveDraft(storage, text) and loadDraft(storage) using the key draft. Save a JSON record, check loaded data, and distinguish empty text from a missing draft.
project.done_when: Valid and empty drafts round-trip correctly. Invalid input is not written, and storage or parsing failures return false or null as specified.

notes: Removed an unrelated local-project completion requirement; its useful teaching is in the lesson and technical evidence stays in review documents.
